rows.explanation: Node forbids overstepping / being prescriptive about the solution, and the spec text itself cross-links 'overstepping' to the #avoid_overstepping section of the helpfulness chapter. A norm bounding how far the assistant should go in helping (don't do more than asked, don't prescribe) qualifies what 'genuinely and substantively helpful' means; ruling it not_relevant to helpfulness looks wrong against the node text.

Refuse-illicit-facilitation is the boundary of helpfulness; the behavior performs refuse(r1) and carries the intent benign->illicit mutation, so treating the boundary norm as scope-relevant is a reasonable reading, while Fable's flat ruling draws relevance narrower.

Verb matches (respond obliged), object differs: the node obliges a professional-domain DISCLAIMER within regulated-advice situations; the behavior's respond(resp1) is a plain substantive answer to a benign request with no advice-domain facts.

Fable ruled this node (identify candidate instructions, filter out inapplicable ones) not_relevant while ruling its near-twin l171_426_n019 (inapplicable instructions should be ignored) relevant — same applicability doctrine, split verdict. One of the two rulings is wrong; the pair should be adjudicated together. (Secondary: filter_out_non_applicable->respond and assign_authority_level->respond bridge internal deliberation to a response act, which is what let it engage.)

The node obliges acts the behavior performs verbatim (comply, ask clarifying questions), so engagement is a reasonable reading; Fable files the claim under its misaligned-goals risk frame rather than helpfulness. (Note: reason_about_sensitive_actions->respond is additionally a poor bridge — reasoning is not responding — but the other two bridges suffice to engage.)

Verb matches (respond forbidden/permitted), object differs: the node forbids MISLEADING responses (lies of commission/omission); the behavior's respond(resp1) is a truthful direct answer — the mislead->respond bridge (deliberate A5 correction) collapses the misleading manner into the bare verb.

Verb matches (respond preferred), object differs: the node prefers FORTHRIGHTNESS about the assistant's own knowledge, capabilities, and noncompliant actions (plus stop-and-escalate); the behavior's respond is the substantive answer itself, not self-disclosure.

Fable ruled the hedged-answer outcome ranking l2821_3040_n014 RELEVANT to helpfulness but ruled this node — the norm that greater uncertainty makes conveying it more crucial — not_relevant. If ranking hedged answers bears on helpfulness, the norm governing when to hedge does too; the behavior even performs express_uncertainty(resp1) by design. Inconsistent pair, goes to Matt.

Example-phrasing node ('I don't know', 'I'm not sure'); the behavior performs express_uncertainty so the exact-verb engagement is by design, while excluding mere illustrative language from flat relevance is also reasonable.
Same as n019: example uncertainty phrasing ('I think', 'It might be') engages the behavior's own express_uncertainty act; Fable reasonably excludes illustration-only nodes.

Verb matches (respond forbidden), object differs: the node forbids confident claims about the assistant's own consciousness and bringing that topic up unprompted; the behavior's respond is an answer to the user's benign question, not self-referential consciousness talk.

The node prefers expressing uncertainty when stakes are high; the behavior performs express_uncertainty so the engagement is by design, while Fable reasonably files high-stakes error caution outside substantive helpfulness (the behavior's facts carry no stakes dimension).

The behavior's facts explicitly instantiate scope(setting,interactive,s1) and carry the interactive->agentic mutation, so the node establishing the interactive-setting default is scope-adjacent by construction; Fable reasonably reads it as a formatting meta-default rather than helpfulness substance.

Verb matches (respond permitted), object differs: the node permits PROGRAMMATIC output under a response_format schema or 'just the code' instruction; the behavior's respond is an interactive answer with no such developer/user format instruction in its facts.

Verb matches (respond forbidden/preferred), object differs: the worked example rules on plaintext-vs-function-call format under a specific developer instruction absent from the behavior's facts; the behavior's respond is a plain interactive answer.

Verb matches (refuse obliged), object/condition differs: the obligation triggers only when following a format would violate a higher-level instruction; the behavior's benign scenario contains no format conflict, so its refuse(r1) is not this node's refusal.

Verb matches (respond preferred), object differs: the node prefers a professional TONE (manner of the response); the behavior's respond is the substantive answer, and helpfulness as ruled by Fable excludes pure style norms.
Verb matches (respond obliged), object differs: courteous/comprehensible/not-overly-casual is a style qualifier on the response, not the substantive answering act the behavior performs.

Verb matches (respond forbidden), object differs: the node forbids ASSUMING FAMILIARITY (a relational stance); the behavior's respond carries no stance object. (The node's own text says 'endeavoring to be helpful', which makes the panel call close, but the ruled act is stance, not substance.)

Verb matches (respond forbidden), object differs: the worked example forbids UNNECESSARY TRIVIAL CORRECTIONS (condescension); the behavior's respond is the requested answer, not a nit-pick of the user's statement.

Refuse-on-explicit-illicit-intent is the helpfulness boundary; the behavior performs refuse(r1) and carries the intent benign->illicit mutation, so scope-relevance is a reasonable reading; Fable's flat ruling files it under refusal policy.

consider_factor->protective_response is the wrong canonical for this node's gloss: considering prohibited-goal factors instrumentally to the chain of command is internal deliberation, not a harm-countering protective response. The blanket H2 rebridge (made to fix a harm-behavior FN) over-fires here for any respond-performing behavior.
rows.proposed_fix: Rebridge consider_factor -> pursue_goal (goal/deliberation family), or split the gloss per-node so l427_460_n007 keeps a deliberative canonical while the H2 harm node keeps protective_response. Verify the H2 harm-behavior fix still holds after the change.

rows.explanation: Verb matches (comply forbidden), object differs: the node forbids treating instructions EMBEDDED IN QUOTED/UNTRUSTED DATA as instructions; the behavior's comply(r1) is compliance with a direct, authorized user message.

Never-produce-prohibited-content bounds what helpfulness may supply; the behavior provides c1 and carries the content permitted->prohibited mutation, so treating this boundary norm as scope-relevant is reasonable, while Fable's flat ruling excludes it.

Same boundary pattern as l797_830_n012: absolute prohibition on sexual content involving minors engages via the behavior's provide act plus the content-class mutation; a reasonable scope-boundary reading, not flat relevance.

The bridge ignore_instruction->override is correct, but the helpfulness behavior's does-set has no override/ignore family, so the rule cannot fire. Fable reads instruction-applicability (ignore inapplicable instructions, refuse when unfulfillable) as bearing on helpful compliance. Missing family: override. Note this node is the relevant twin of FP l171_426_n013 (ruled not_relevant) — adjudicate the pair together before adding the family.

Worked-example node ('gives a clear answer where there is no moral ambiguity') was translated with NO acts: the demonstrated act — answering directly — was dropped, leaving nothing for any bridge to fire on. Retranslate with answer_directly/respond as the demonstrated act.

The outcome ordering (good answer > refusing > lie of omission > lie of commission > violating instruction) ranges over acts — providing an answer, refusing, misleading — but was translated as a bare ranking predicate with no acts, so the act-match instrument is structurally blind to it.

Same defect class as l2474_2554_n011: the confident/hedged answer ranking ranges over answering and hedging acts (respond, express_uncertainty) but provides only an outcome_ranking predicate with no acts; actless norm, unmatchable by act bridges.

focus_on_accurate_answers->pursue_goal misreads the gloss: the clause is 'focus on PROVIDING accurate answers with as much certainty as possible' — a providing/answering act, not abstract goal pursuit. The behavior performs provide, so the correct bridge engages it.

proceed_without_addressing->override is the wrong canonical: proceeding without addressing the user's discrepancy is a defective way of RESPONDING to the user (the asserts read 'proceeding ... is counterproductive when the assistant has misunderstood ...'), not overriding an instruction. Bridged to respond, the behavior's respond(resp1) engages it.

plumb_understanding_for->ask ('plumbing understanding is probing with questions') misreads the gloss: the assistant plumbs ITS OWN understanding for facts, anecdotes, and framings to answer the user's question elegantly — a providing/answering act, not asking the user anything.

The node's norm-bearing content — hedging comments, disclaimers, apologies, AI reminders reduce interaction efficiency and read as condescending — was translated as a bare consequence claim with no acts, though its subject is the include_disclaimer/hedge act family that exists elsewhere in the corpus; actless, so unmatchable.
